To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Ca2+ and length-dependent activation of insect fibrilllar muscle can be explained by a simple mechanical model.
the ATPase activity of insect flight muscle increases as a result of either an increase in Ca2+ or an increase in fibre extension.

(1) the rate of Ca 2+-activated ATPase activity of insect fibrilllar muscle is increased by small degrees of elongation, (2) this increase in activity is accompanied by an increased Ca 2+ uptake, (3) the effect of elongation on the Ca 2+-ATPase is not observed in glycerinated muscle from frog sartorious and rabbit psoas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of oscillating contraction in the flight muscles of insects.
the mechanism by which calcium ions (Ca2+) activate the contractile mechanism in insect fibrillar (flight) muscle.
the mechanism of oscillating contraction in insect fibrillar (fibrillar) flight muscle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ca 2+-activated ATPase of insect fibrilllar flight muscle is increased in activity by small length changes.
the Ca 2+-activated ATPase activity in insect fibrillar fibres increases when the A filament lattice is stretched, presumably by a direct mechanical effect on the Ca2+ binding sites.
the Ca 2+-activated ATPase is activated by Ca 2+ ions and by the elongation of the A filament in insect fibrillar muscles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ca 2+ activates the ATPase and fibre extension increases the Ca 2 + sensitivity of the ATPase.
in the insect fibrillar muscles studied, the Ca 2+-activated ATPase activity is increased by small maintained fibre elongations.
in insect fibrillar muscles the Ca2+-activated ATPase is activated not only by Ca2+ binding but also by the stretching of the actin filaments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we found that the effect of Ca2 + and fibre elongation is not limited to the activation of the ATPase activity in the absence of any other factor.
we have shown that the effect of Ca2 + and fibre elongation is not only on the contractile mechanism but also on the ATPase activity of the muscle.
the Ca2+ sensitivity of insect flight muscle is increased by small degrees of fibre elongation.
